provider: git-annex rclone special remote (built into annex since 2023)

free_tier.stated: N/A — front-end to rclone's ~70 backends, so it inherits every free tier already catalogued by the other C-slots. The docs' own list (still current) names Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Mega, pCloud, Box, Yandex, Jottacloud, WebDAV, FTP, SFTP, Swift, B2, S3.

egress.terms: rclone throttles/retries but does not pay for egress.

tooling: Two paths: (a) `git annex initremote type=rclone ...` — native, no extra install, documented via `rclone gitannex -h`; (b) the older `git-annex-remote-rclone` bash script (DanielDent, ~300 lines). rclone itself is a single static binary.
chaining: The strongest multiplier in this slot: annex gives you versioning + hash verification + partial clone, rclone gives you ~70 free-tier backends. One annex repo can have a dozen rclone remotes across a dozen free accounts of different providers, with `git annex copy --to` fanning out. This is literally the 'google-drive-service-account' pattern applied to large-file versioning.
limits_note: Per-backend: file size caps, per-day upload quotas, API rate limits all apply unchanged. rclone's Drive backend has its own 750 GB/day upload cap; OneDrive throttles. Encrypted annex remotes lose rclone's server-side dedupe.

reliability_note: Solid; the native remote removed the bash-script dependency. The failure mode is per-backend token expiry and drive-level rate limiting, which rclone surfaces as retries rather than data loss.
